    AI Overview
    The Artemis 2 rocket, known as the Space Launch System (SLS), is a NASA program primarily built by major aerospace contractors. Boeing built the massive core stage, Northrop Grumman provided the solid rocket boosters, and United Launch Alliance built the Interim Cryogenic Propulsion System upper stage. 
    This video shows a closer look at the components and build of the Artemis II rocket:
    1m
    VideoFromSpace
    YouTube• Mar 30, 2026
    Key Manufacturer Roles for Artemis II: 
    • Core Stage (Boeing): Developed at NASA's Michoud Assembly Facility, this stage is the largest part of the rocket, featuring four RS-25 engines.
    • Boosters (Northrop Grumman): These are 5-segment solid rocket boosters derived from the Space Shuttle program.
    • Upper Stage (United Launch Alliance - ULA): The Interim Cryogenic Propulsion System (ICPS) provides the final push to the Moon.
    • Engines (Aerojet Rocketdyne): Built the RS-25 engines for the core stage.
    • Orion Spacecraft (Lockheed Martin): While not technically the rocket, the crew capsule for Artemis 2 is built by Lockheed Martin. 
    This video introduces the Orion spacecraft, which will carry the crew during the Artemis II mission:
    50s
